(1) repeated ECS significantly attenuates the depressive influence of intra-hipocampally microinjected clonidine upon rat activity in the open field, (2) chemical lesions to the median raphé nucleus (MR) significantly potentiate the stimulatory effects of clonidine injected into the same brain structure upon rat active behaviour in the forced swimming test, and (3) the effects of clonidin in the open field may be mediated by neuronal structures other than those involved
repeated ECS and chemical depletion of central serotonin do not significantly affect the adaptive processes in alpha 2-adrenergic receptors in the hippocampus.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of central serotonin in the adaptive processes occurring at the alpha 2-adenoreceptor in the course of the treatment with tricylic antidepressant and ECS, as well as with the possible involvement of serotonin in the clonidine effects on the rat behaviour.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ECS-induced changes in behavioural activity of intra-hipocampally microinjected clonidine may be related to the adaptive processes occurring within the hippocampal serotoninergic system.
the role of central serotonin in the adaptive processes in the alpha 1- and alpha 2-adrenergic systems in the rat hippocampus is not yet clear.
the ECS-induced changes in the behavioural effects of clonidine are not related to serotonin depletion in the rat brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of brain serotonin system in the antidepressant-like activity of clonidine in these two tests is rather limited and it may depend on the behavioural test used and/or the brain area involved.
the behavioural effects of clonidine are dependent on the state of the central nervous system, and they are not mediated by serotoninergic mechanisms.
ECS-induced changes in the behavioural activity of clonidine in these two tests may be mediated, at least partly, by different mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hippocampal alpha 2-adrenoreceptors are probably involved in the regulation of the adaptive processes in the central nervous system, which are induced by repeated electroconvulsive shock.
the effects of clonidine in both tests are not mediated by central serotonin.
the effects of serotonin depletion in the hippocampus may be dependent on the behavioural task and on the experimental conditions.
